title: Cookies and Cream Custard Ice Cream
changes_from_base: Extra vanilla and slightly less yolk for a very white base, with broken chocolate sandwich cookies folded in at the end.
summary: Our classic French custard with extra vanilla and slightly fewer yolks for a whiter base, then packed with broken chocolate sandwich cookies after churning. The real-custard version of a favourite.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
chocolate sandwich cookies (cream-filled), broken into chunks

steps.title: Heat the milk
steps.text: Warm the milk and half the cream in the saucepan until steaming. Pour the other half of the cream into a bowl sitting in the iced water.

steps.title: Whisk the yolks
steps.text: Whisk the yolks, sugar and salt until pale.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Slowly whisk in a third of the hot milk, then tip everything back into the pan.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Cook on low, stirring all the time, until the thermometer shows 77-80 °C and a line drawn through the coating holds.

steps.title: Cool fast
steps.text: Strain the custard straight into the cold cream, which stops it cooking, and stir in the vanilla. Chill for at least 4 h.

steps.title: Break the cookies
steps.text: Break the cookies into uneven chunks, some large and some small, and chill them.

steps.title: Churn and fold
steps.text: Churn until thick, fold in the cookie chunks and freeze for at least 3 h.

tips: Leaving some chunks large gives the classic look; crumbs alone turn it grey.
A common mistake is adding the cookies too early in the machine, where they get ground to dust.
If it has been frozen overnight, let it soften for 15 min before scooping.
storage: Freeze in a covered container for up to 2 weeks; the cookies soften gradually.
